content.comment_body: What actions should be taken if a [product_name] without display no longer allows [product_name] software access due to a forgotten password? With a [product_name] that includes a display, it can be reset to factory settings via the device menu. Without a display, only a reset via [product_name] software is possible, but this requires the password. It would be helpful if the development team provided guidance, even through an FAQ. Perhaps the moderator could forward this concern to the appropriate department.
There’s another issue: if the base module with display is switched from admin to operator mode but the admin password is set and then forgotten, it also creates a lockout situation.
Correct. These are two separate scenarios, but both result in the same situation: no [product_name] software access without the password.

The password for '[product_name] software & web editor access' can only be changed if you know it. This password only affects remote access. A tool is planned that will allow a full factory reset including all passwords, requiring a Micro SD card. However, I cannot confirm its release.

That information isn’t entirely accurate. After resetting my [product_name] to factory settings, access via [product_name] software and web editor does not prompt for a password unless password protection is activated. If you enable protection but leave the default password, it is 'LOGO'. When password protection is active, a password prompt appears for both remote and local access regardless of whether the password is default or changed.

This should really be addressed by the development team. It is concerning that there hasn’t been a tool available or why such a bug passed functional testing. The device has been on the market for years, and [company_name] is only now considering improvements. Is this due to lack of funding or insufficient attention to product support?
The reset tool has now been released. See this topic: Reset Tool for restoring [product_name] to its original state.

There is another approach if you have the [product_name] program on your PC but forgot your password: Right-click on the program and select Edit with Notepad++. If it displays readable text, you may find the password within the file. If it shows only symbols, password recovery might not be possible unless someone has a way to decrypt them. Good luck with your search!
This method does not work because the password for [product_name] software access is not stored in the software file—it is only stored on the device itself.

I tend to disagree; I use [product_name] software and it works for me. If you load your project in diagram mode, you may find your password, but if you set up your project as a network project and add a device, you won’t find it. Also, when saving your project in diagram mode, the file extension is *.lsc, while in network project mode, it’s *.lnp—different file types.

Well, you may have more experience than I do. The password for software and web editor access is set via access control, not file properties. To change or activate password protection for software access, you must connect to the device online. The process for saving programs (diagram or network project) has been the same since software version [version_no]. That's nothing new to me.

I spent two days trying, and the solution was only accessible via an operator panel; you can restore the base module without a display to factory settings through the panel. The program isn’t recovered, but at least you regain the controller.
Please post messages in English. English is the preferred language here.

Not everyone has an operator panel available. Many people purchase the version without display for a reason, not intending to buy a panel just in case they forget their password. The reset tool was created for this scenario.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced a significant lockout issue with the [product_name] without display when the software access password was forgotten. The inability to reset the device using its menu makes recovery difficult, and early tools did not resolve the problem without the password. Various opinions were shared about password storage and recovery methods. Frustration was expressed over the late development and release of a comprehensive reset tool, but its eventual availability was seen as a positive step. Users also expected greater transparency and quicker response from [company_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a secure yet straightforward method to reset or restore access to [product_name] devices without display when passwords are forgotten. Prompt support and clear, timely communication about available solutions are also expected.
